I keep thinking as we inch closer to the October 1yr anniversary, it was the same week of my rape and kidnapping that the Harvey Weinstein news broke. The same moment the #MeToo movement had its resurgence.
In October there will be a million #MeToo think pieces. They'll ask things like "where are we one year later?" and "what has changed?", etc...

So much has changed in one year, so much has changed in 10 months. However, and this is too often the case for victims, our lives change dramatically, but the people who harmed us...their lives continue as if nothing happened.
#MeToo

I think about this a lot: would an apology make me feel better? What does an apology mean? I think an apology would only make the abuser feel better? An apology is an acknowledgment of harm, but it can also act as closure for the person who caused the harm. #MeToo

An apology can sometimes make the person who harmed you assume they're absolved, their hands are washed clean, they're done, they don't need to do any more work. So I don't want an apology from you, you still have SO MUCH more work to do. #MeToo

Also, I've been thinking a lot about what happens when someone apologizes to you. They expect, want, or need you to respond in a certain way. They want you to say "I forgive you". The person harmed has to do the labor to make the abuser feel better. #MeToo

So I hope as we see, as we publish, and as we support all these men coming forward and "apologizing" and absolving themselves of this guilt we think about all the people they've harmed and where they are, what they're doing, how they're doing. #MeToo
